newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mubarak to Jordan for Mideast peace crisis talks.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak to Jordan for Mideast peace crisis talks.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak left for Jordan on Saturday for talks with King Hussein on ways to break the logjam in the Middle East peace process.
Airport officials said Mubarak was flying to the Jordanian Red Sea port of Aqaba, where he was to meet the king ahead of a visit to Egypt by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday.
Palestinian-Israeli peace talks have been deadlocked since March, when Israel approved construction of a controversial Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem.

The Palestinians say talks can resume only after Israel stops work on the settlement on a hill Jews call Har Homa and Arabs call Jabal Abu Ghneim. Egypt, which considers itself an unofficial sponsor of the peace talks, supports their view.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat held talks with Mubarak on Wednesday and Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said in remarks broadcast on Friday that the Mubarak-Netanyahu summit would succeed if Israel agreed to stop the building.
Both Egypt and Jordan have peace treaties with Israel but ties between Amman and the Jewish state are much stronger than those linking Cairo and Israel.
